rubrics.justification: Describes a good-quality expanded/full blastocyst with thinning zona, compact ICM, and cohesive TE consistent with the reported AA morphology; appropriately notes limits of a single static image. Minor issue in questioning 3AA vs 4AA without image certainty.

Thoroughly integrates age, diagnosis, BMI, FSH, endometrial thickness, prior IVF history, sperm parameters, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis, while distinguishing transfer prognosis from future cycle planning.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent, with probability estimates tied to embryo quality and patient factors. Small limitation is somewhat broad success-rate framing and slight ambiguity between implantation and clinical pregnancy rates.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF best practice: favorable prognosis, SET at age 31 with a high-grade blastocyst, caution about overinterpreting morphology, and no extensive workup after one failed transfer. Minor deviation is loose handling of Gardner stage terminology.

Provides practical next steps for transfer management, lifestyle, luteal support review, and future evaluation if unsuccessful. Useful and nuanced, though some recommendations remain general rather than protocol-specific.
